name: Chamarajanagara
headline: Tribal customs and seasonal migration are blamed for secondary exits; only three child marriages reported in 2025.
summary: A Times of India report on a legislative reply names Chamarajanagara as one of two tribal-dominated districts where social customs are blamed for school dropout. Reported child marriages were only three in the first ten months of 2025.

reasons.factor: Social customs in a tribal-dominated district
reasons.detail: In a legislative reply, social customs were blamed as one reason for dropout in two tribal-dominated districts, Chamarajanagara and Chitradurga.
Counselling by teachers and officials identified domestic problems and severe poverty as the main reasons for dropout in the 2024 survey.

reasons.factor: Parents sending children to field work
reasons.detail: About 30 cases were found where parents made children leave school to work in fields; absenteeism is also reported in the MM Hills area.
Children sell puja items, flowers and incense around festivals at the Male Mahadeshwara Hills area, drawing them away from classes.
Of 19 ashrama schools serving Soliga and other tribal communities, most lie inside forests; teacher recruitment has stalled and Covid closures pushed families towards tobacco picking.
An expert cites poor academic environment, weak home support, remote living and social prejudice affecting adolescents; 101 ST dropouts were reported in the district.
Pass rate fell to 61.4% in 2025 and rank to 27th; no direct link to dropout was reported.

headlines.takeaway: Also reports 101 ST dropouts in Chamarajanagar including 38 girls; expert points to remote hamlets and weak school access.

headlines.takeaway: Chamarajanagar's pass rate fell from 71.6% to 61.4%, dropping its rank from 24th to 27th.

headlines.title: Chamarajanagar district faces alarmingly high school dropout rates
headlines.takeaway: Education department found 128 dropouts, led by Hanur; poverty and parents pushing children into field work cited.

headlines.title: 100 out of 228 dropout children return to school
headlines.takeaway: Officials identified 228 dropouts and brought about 100 back, using counselling and monitoring of families forcing children to work.

headlines.title: Bleak future ahead: COVID-19 pushes Karnataka's first generation Adivasi learners off schools
headlines.takeaway: Covers Chamarajanagar's 19 ashrama schools, stalled teacher hiring, lost connectivity and increased tobacco-picking labour.

responses.text: Teachers and officials counselled families and monitored those working in neighbouring districts; about 100 of 228 identified dropouts returned to school in 2024.
The district has added government schools in tribal and hilly areas, according to the Patrika report.

Medium of instruction is not documented as a barrier here.
